title: FirstMate workflow definition
description: A workflow is a small state machine of named steps. `bin/fm-workflow validate` enforces this schema (its structural half is evaluated by a jq subset validator, so no schema library is needed) plus the rules a schema cannot express: roles exist and can produce the step's output (roles/manifest.json), every transition target exists, every outcome of a step is routed, every step is reachable, and every cycle passes through a loop that has a limit. `x-outcomes`, `x-attrs` and `x-gates` are non-standard keywords read by the engine: the outcomes each output contract can produce, the run attributes a transition may branch on, and the gates a definition can set to observe or enforce.

version.description: Bump on every behavior change; a running task keeps the version it started with (its state file pins the definition).

when.description: What kind of task selects this workflow: the Captain's selection guidance, read by `fm-workflow list`.

roles.description: Alias -> role under roles/. Steps bind to an alias, so swapping the agent for a kind of work is one edit here; the role's manifest `outputs` must include the output of every step bound to it.

gates.description: Engine gates over the structured final blocks. Absent = observe: the engine records `would-block` and lets the result through. enforce: the step is re-run with the problems as feedback; after two blocks of the same gate in one run the third is let through and recorded `escaped` (a gate must never wedge a run). evidence: a done result shows >=1 command with observed output (and base+commit when the step commits). answers: every open feedback id is answered fixed or rejected. commit: a verdict or risk block names the head commit of the change it judged. coverage: a verifier accounts for every finding it was handed.

when.description: Branch on a run attribute set by a risk step (x-attrs). Every key must match one of its values.

target.description: A step name; the reserved @complete (the workflow succeeded), @escalate (stop and hand the accumulated feedback to the captain) or @close (the task is deliberately closed: no delivery); {to, loop} to take the transition inside a named loop; or a list of alternatives [{to, when}..., {to}] where the first whose `when` matches the run attributes is taken and the last has no `when`.

maxIterations.description: How many times a transition tagged with this loop may be taken. The attempt after that is not taken: onExhausted applies. Review and verification loops use 3: after three rounds the author steps back instead of taking a fourth.

resets.description: Taking a transition tagged with this loop resets the counters of the listed other loops: a reshaped approach starts with fresh rounds (otherwise a reshape after a round cap would be exhausted at once).

onExhausted.description: Never a silent stop and never a silent pass. "escalate" hands the accumulated feedback to the captain. {"to": step} routes to a step-back step instead (the author reconsiders the approach with every accumulated finding); that step must itself end in change-direction or escalate.

from.description: task: the task text the workflow was started with. change: the commit range under work (base..head, from the last result that gave a commit). delta: the commits since the last commit the consuming step itself judged, up to the current head (diff-only re-review); omitted when that step has not judged a commit yet, so its first run reviews the whole change. report: the latest recorded report of `step`. feedback: the latest still-open feedback list produced by any of `steps`, verbatim. feedback-all: every feedback list ever produced by `steps`, open or closed, verbatim (the step-back step). direction: the latest change-direction raised by any step. notes: the non-blocking notes (OPTIONAL, PRE-EXISTING) recorded so far. risk: the latest risk classification. decision: the choice and the stated reason of the latest decision recorded at the decision step `step` (what an amend asks to change).

optional.description: Omit the input silently when nothing is available yet (feedback on a first run).

kind.description: work: a worker with the step's role runs it. decision: the orchestrator decides, by the stated criteria. deliver: Firstmate delivers through the task's own delivery mode; it is never a role.

role.description: A key of the workflow's roles map (work steps only).

output.description: report: free-form report; the orchestrator records its status line as the outcome (done, blocked or change-direction). result: the report ends with the fenced `result` block; the outcome is its status, parsed by the engine. verdict: the report ends with the fenced `verdict` block; the outcome is parsed, never supplied by the caller. risk: the report ends with the fenced `risk` block; the outcome is its tier and it sets the run attributes. A malformed result or risk block is re-run (twice, then blocked); a malformed verdict is a FAIL.

commits.description: result steps only: the step commits work to the task branch, so its result carries base and commit (the evidence gate checks it) and the engine tracks the change range.

verifies.description: verdict steps only: the verdict steps whose findings this step must account for (coverage gate). It consumes their open feedback; only the findings it confirms go back to the implementer.

on.description: Outcome -> target. A work step routes every outcome of its output contract (x-outcomes), change-direction included: a wrong approach is raised early as an explicit outcome, never ground through; a deliver step routes done and blocked; a decision step's keys are its choices.
